source.title: Sparse Feature Circuits: Discovering and Editing Interpretable Causal Graphs in Language Models
source.authors: Samuel Marks; C. Rager; Eric J. Michaud; Yonatan Belinkov; David Bau; Aaron Mueller

page_placements.theme: Dictionary features and other non-neuron directions (SAE, NMF, PCA, codes, CAVs, optimised neuron combinations) are more interpretable or concept-selective than native neurons

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether circuits made from a model’s own neurons can account for behavior, using circuit faithfulness and completeness measures rather than the claim’s original audit method.
record.gate_note: The study does not measure what share of neuron poles have one or two main jobs, nor test the other claim versions. It reports human interpretability ratings for neurons and SAE features, and neuron-circuit evaluations on subject–verb agreement. Values shown only in Figure 3 are not separately extracted unless described in the text. Cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study builds circuits from the model's own neurons (no SAE, so no error terms) in Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B and measures faithfulness and completeness on held-out subject–verb agreement data. It also tries neuron-based circuit editing on Bias in Bios. These results bear directly on whether neurons suffice as circuit units (V5). The neuron circuits are the paper's baseline, but their own numbers are reported and bear on V5. No other version is tested: human ratings are mean 0–100 scores, not shares of neurons with one job.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that neurons are polysemantic and rarely interpretable, making neuron circuits unsuitable for downstream use. Sparse SAE feature circuits are more interpretable and more compact: far fewer nodes explain or remove agreement behaviour. Feature-based ablation (SHIFT) removes a classifier's gender reliance far better than a neuron-based skyline.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SAE-based feature circuits and neuron-circuit baselines, with causal faithfulness/completeness evaluations and human interpretability ratings; it does not perform the pole-by-pole audit described in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The circuit-size comparisons differ between Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B. The study also evaluates several subject–verb agreement structures, but the text does not give separate numerical neuron-circuit size results for each structure.

fits_no_version.finding: In Pythia-70M, crowdworkers gave neurons mean interpretability ratings of 30–36 on a 0–100 scale, against 53–82 for SAE features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Human raters judge small-model neurons less interpretable on average than SAE features; this is a mean rating, not a share of neurons with one job.

record.problems: The neuron-circuit evaluations concern subject–verb agreement in two models, not a broad audit across models or behaviors. Human interpretability judgments are qualitative and the authors note that annotator selection influenced results. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the tabulated ratings or the stated neuron counts.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible reported results omitted. Figure 3 includes additional curve values that are not stated numerically in the text and were not read off the plot.

untested.parts: Pole-level audit shares (90/7/2–4%) in Qwen3-32B; not tested.
Shares of interpretable neurons across dense and MoE models up to trillions of parameters; not tested.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron, pose, recursive generalization versus superposition; not tested.
Architecture, regularization and tools as causes of neuron interpretability, and the vision-model share estimates; not tested.
Large models (only 70M and 2B tested), attribution graphs for behaviours beyond agreement and the Bias in Bios classifier, and a direct comparison to replacement-model reconstruction error.
Held-out prediction of where neurons fire from activating-example explanations; not tested.
Simulation-based automated scoring of neuron explanations; not tested.

missing.what: Neuron skyline results on Bias in Bios: Pythia 75.5 profession / 73.2 gender / 41.5 worst group; Gemma 65.1 / 84.3 / 5.6. Feature-based SHIFT and feature skyline comparisons sit alongside.
Statement that SHIFT with neurons was abandoned because essentially none of the neurons were interpretable, with example uninterpretable neurons.
Neuron-circuit faithfulness and completeness curves per agreement structure and at maximum size.

record.verdict_notes: The models are small (70M, 2B), so V5's 'large model' setting is not reached. The neuron circuits are the paper's baseline, not its own method, but they are the only results bearing on V5. The reader's 'supports' label from r3–r4 is dropped: needing hundreds to thousands of neurons to remove performance does not show neurons are adequate circuit units. Gemma neuron interpretability was not rated; the paper defers to Gemma Scope for SAE features only.

versions.untested_parts: The share of neuron poles with one or two jobs, and the share not understood.
Other model sizes and architectures, dense versus mixture-of-experts models, and scaling up to trillions of parameters.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose, recursive generalization, and superposition.
Architecture, regularization, tool quality as causes of interpretability differences, and the stated InceptionV1-sized model estimates.

Tests neuron-based circuits on subject–verb agreement in Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B; does not test attribution graphs across other behaviors or larger models, or separately evaluate the claim’s phrasing about avoiding a trained replacement model.
Whether explanations based on activating examples predict where a neuron fires on held-out activations.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

relationships.condition: Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B, subject–verb agreement, neuron circuits evaluated on held-out pairs
relationships.reason: Neuron circuits are causally faithful only at large size: about 1500 / 50000 neurons explain half the performance. Removing performance takes hundreds / thousands of neurons, versus a few feature nodes (r1–r4).
relationships.display_finding: Neuron circuits were causally faithful only when large: explaining half the performance took about 1500 / 50000 neurons, and removing it took hundreds / thousands of neurons, versus a few feature nodes.

relation.reason: Neuron circuit faithfulness and completeness results bear directly on V5.

tranche.reason: Different method (SAE and neuron circuits, faithfulness/completeness) on the same question of whether neurons suffice as circuit units.

source_check.notes: The text defines 'neuron' as a basis-aligned direction (fn. 1) in the same sublayers as the SAEs: MLP, residual stream, attention out-projection. On SVA, nodes are counted per token position (App. A.2), so '50000 neurons' means neuron-position nodes. This matters when comparing with 2601.22594's MLP-activation neurons. BiB results (Table 2, §4, App. D.2) have no rows; Table 7 ratings are Pythia-70M only.

statements.correction: Label should be limits_scope. Facts: SHIFT with neurons was abandoned because essentially none of the neurons are interpretable (§4; App. D.2, Figs 21-22). The neuron skyline mean-ablates 55 (Pythia) or 43 (Gemma) neurons chosen using the balanced set (an unfair advantage). Worst-group accuracy: 41.5 vs SHIFT 76.0 (Pythia-70M); 5.6 vs 50.0 (Gemma-2-2B; original classifier 18.2). Crowdworker mean rating of top-30 BiB neurons: 36.0/100 (Pythia only, Table 7).
statements.problem: All numbers match Table 2 and the §4 text. The App. D.2 / Figs 21-22 citation is fine: these are the authors' own judgments that the BiB neurons can't be interpreted. The label 'challenges' is wrong. The setting is small models (70M, 2B), no BiB neuron circuit is tested for faithfulness, and the evidence is a qualitative interpretability call plus an editing skyline. That qualifies V5; it does not show the effect absent where V5 says it should hold.

statements.correction: Fn. 1: 'neuron' means a basis-aligned direction in the latent space, not necessarily after a nonlinearity. Neuron circuits apply the same method with neurons in place of SAE features (§3.2), in the same sublayers: MLPs, layer-end residual stream and attention out-projection (App. D.2). Attribution uses linear approximations to the indirect effect (attribution patching / integrated gradients, §2-3.1), not RelP. Evaluation uses mean ablation. On SVA, nodes are counted per token position (App. A.2). Gemma-2-2B: about 50000 neurons for half the performance vs 500 feature nodes for the majority; thousands of neurons vs a few feature nodes to remove performance.
statements.problem: The numbers are right. But the entry treats the neuron basis and attribution method as unknown, and the text gives them, which bears directly on this conflict. Also, the Gemma comparator for half the performance is about 500 feature nodes, not 'a few'; 'a few' applies only to completeness.

statements.correction: 2403.19647: neuron-circuit faithfulness was measured only on SVA (about 1500 / 50000 neurons for half the performance). Interpretability was low on both tasks: Pythia-70M top-30 agreement neurons rated 30.2/100, BiB neurons 36.0/100, random neurons 32.6 (Table 7). There is no task contrast within this study.
statements.problem: Under factor 'Task', the 2403.19647 sentence suggests that neurons work on SVA but not on BiB. In this study the contrast is between measures, not tasks. Faithfulness was measured only on SVA, and SVA circuit neurons were also rated poorly.

statements.correction: 2403.19647 verdicts: limits_scope on SVA (neuron circuits faithful only at about 1500 neurons in Pythia-70M and about 50000 in Gemma-2-2B; hundreds or thousands of neurons to remove performance). limits_scope on BiB (neurons judged essentially uninterpretable in 70M/2B models; neuron skyline trails SHIFT).
statements.problem: It says 2403.19647 challenges V5, citing both the BiB result and the 50000-neuron SVA result. The SVA result is a limits_scope verdict (l0), and the BiB verdict should also be limits_scope, so this study gives no challenge and the challenges count drops by one.

statements.correction: BiB verdict: limits_scope. Neurons are basis-aligned directions, not necessarily post-nonlinearity (fn. 1), taken from MLPs, the layer-end residual stream and the attention out-projection (App. D.2). Attribution: attribution patching / integrated-gradient approximations to the indirect effect, with mean ablation. SVA nodes are counted per token position (App. A.2).
statements.problem: The numbers are right (Table 2; Table 7 30.2-36.0 vs 52.8-81.5). But it calls the study the 'main V5 challenge' and gives a challenges verdict, which should be limits_scope. Its 'still open' item (neuron basis and attribution method) is answered in the text.
